# Video script: Refer or not?

> DRAFT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE. Contains claims with status 'ai-extracted' that no clinician has verified.

Unit D11 | Target length: 5 min

| # | Shot | Narration | Claims |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Presenter to camera | You do not need a diagnosis to refer. A suspicion is enough. | IS23-078 |
| 2 | Graphic: list of fetal indications appearing one by one | From the scan: a suspected heart anomaly, another anomaly linked to the heart, a large or poorly working heart, hydrops, a rate that stays too slow or too fast, an irregular rhythm that persists, a thick nuchal translucency. | IS23-082 |
| 3 | Graphic: list of maternal and family indications | From the history: heart disease in a parent or sibling of this fetus, diabetes before pregnancy, anti-Ro antibodies, phenylketonuria, retinoids, a confirmed fetal infection. | IS23-083 |
| 4 | Graphic: 'not enough evidence' list | And the ones where the evidence for raised risk is not enough: an isolated bright spot in the heart, a single umbilical artery on its own, soft markers outside the heart. | IS23-085 |
| 5 | Presenter | Most babies with heart disease have no risk factor. The screen you do on every patient is what finds them. | IS23-080 |
